MIGHTYGUARD.Name: Mighty Guard
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.Detection.Name: Mighty Guard: what counts as damage
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.Detection.Hint: "Damage rolls only" uses the game system's own damage rolls (dnd5e and pf2e supported directly; other systems are detected by roll labels). "Any non-d20 roll" minimizes every roll without a d20 made while targeting a guarded creature — use this if damage isn't being caught in your system.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.Pulse.Name: Spectral glow
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.Pulse.Hint: Tokens with Mighty Guard get a spectral look: a bright cyan rim, glowing blue cracks across the token, a blue tint and rising wisps. Turn off to show only the shield icon (this setting is per player).
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.PulseSeconds.Name: Glow speed (seconds per pulse)
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.PulseSeconds.Hint: How long one full breath of the spectral glow takes. Higher is slower. Takes effect immediately.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.CoverFog.Name: Fog on creatures in cover or hiding
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.CoverFog.Hint: Tokens with a cover status (Half, Three-Quarters or Total Cover) or Hiding are shrouded in slowly swirling fog, thicker for heavier cover. Turn off to hide it (this setting is per player).
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.SleepZs.Name: Floating Z's on sleeping or unconscious creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.SleepZs.Hint: Tokens with the Sleeping or Unconscious condition show green Z's drifting up from them. Turn off to hide them (this setting is per player).
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.MightyGuard: Damage rolls made against this creature roll their minimum.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Haste:
Applied automatically: Speed doubled, +2 bonus to Armor Class, Advantage on Dexterity saving throws.

Remember: the creature gains an additional action on each of its turns. That action can be used only to take the Attack (one attack only), Dash, Disengage, Hide, or Utilize action.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Slow:
Applied automatically: Speed halved, −2 penalty to Armor Class and Dexterity saving throws.

Remember: the creature can't take Reactions. On its turns it can take either an action or a Bonus Action, not both, and it can make only one attack if it takes the Attack action. If it casts a spell with a Somatic component, there is a 25 percent chance the spell fails.

It repeats the Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.MotionOutline.Name: Animated Haste / Slow outlines
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.MotionOutline.Hint: Hasted tokens get a crackling green outline with running highlights and sparks; Slowed tokens (the Slow spell, or Monsters of Drakkenheim's Slowed) get the same in dark blue. Turn off to hide them (this setting is per player).
MIGHTYGUARD.HiddenStatuses.Name: Status palette icons
MIGHTYGUARD.HiddenStatuses.Label: Choose Visible Statuses
MIGHTYGUARD.HiddenStatuses.Hint: Hide status effects you don't use from the token's status palette. The palette shrinks to fit the icons that remain.
MIGHTYGUARD.HiddenStatuses.Title: Visible Status Effects
MIGHTYGUARD.HiddenStatuses.Instructions: Untick a status to hide it from the token status palette for everyone. Hidden statuses still work when applied by spells, items or macros, and still show on tokens.
MIGHTYGUARD.Guidance.Label: Guidance
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.GuidanceCheckbox.Hi: Show a Guidance checkbox under the Situational Bonus field when rolling ability, skill, tool or initiative checks. Ticking it adds 1d4 to the roll.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.CharmHearts.Name: Floating hearts on charmed creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.CharmHearts.Hint: Tokens with the Charmed condition show pink hearts drifting up from them. Turn off to hide them (this setting is per player).
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.BleedingFx.Name: Dripping blood on bleeding creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.BleedingFx.Hint: A streak of blood runs along the bottom of a bleeding creature's token; drops swell at the ends of its drips, fall and splat on the ground below. Per player.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.PoisonedFx.Name: Toxic bubbles on poisoned creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.PoisonedFx.Hint: Tokens with the Poisoned condition get toxic green bubbles rising inside them, a low green haze and a sickly tint. Per player.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.BurningFx.Name: Fiery aura on burning creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.BurningFx.Hint: Tokens with the Burning condition are surrounded by a flickering fiery aura with rising embers. Per player.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.RestrainedFx.Name: Rope on restrained creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.RestrainedFx.Hint: Tokens with the Restrained condition get rope wound around them. Per player.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.StunnedFx.Name: Circling stars on stunned creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.StunnedFx.Hint: Tokens with the Stunned condition have a ring of stars slowly circling their head. Per player.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.PetrifiedFx.Name: Cracked stone on petrified creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.PetrifiedFx.Hint: Tokens with the Petrified condition turn to grey stone, with chiselled cracks, a grainy texture and dust trickling from the cracks. Per player.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.ParalyzedFx.Name: Electric arcs on paralyzed creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.ParalyzedFx.Hint: Tokens with the Paralyzed condition have an arc of lightning across them that holds its shape for a moment, then fades into a new one. Per player.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.DiseasedFx.Name: Sores on diseased creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.DiseasedFx.Hint: Tokens with the Diseased condition get sores that swell and burst, a sickly haze and a sallow tint. Per player.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.IncapacitatedFx.Nam: Drained, fading look on incapacitated creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.IncapacitatedFx.Hin: The token's colour drains to grey and it slowly fades in and out, as if barely there, with a faint, weak heartbeat pulse. Not shown when the creature is also Paralyzed, Petrified, Stunned or Unconscious, which have their own animations.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.FrightenedFx.Name: Shadow tendrils on frightened creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.FrightenedFx.Hint: Tokens with the Frightened condition have writhing black tendrils reaching in from their edge, and a cold, pale tint. Per player.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.ConcentrationFx.Hin: Tokens that are Concentrating have two slowly turning rings of glowing runes around them, with motes of light drawn inward. Per player.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.HideAnimatedIcons.N: Hide status icons for animated statuses
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.HideAnimatedIcons.H: Leave the small status icon off a token when that status is shown by one of this module's animations. If you turn an animation off, its icon comes back. Per player.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.GrappledFx.Name: Clawed grip on grappled creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.GrappledFx.Hint: Tokens with the Grappled condition are gripped by a painted clawed hand whose claws dig over their edge. Per player.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.GrappleImage.Name: Grappled overlay image
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.GrappleImage.Hint: The art used for Grappled (defaults to the bundled clawed hand). Pick any PNG or WebP with a transparent background to use your own; it's centred on the creature. Clear it to use the simple drawn talons instead.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.InvisibleWhirl.Name: Invisible and Ethereal creatures show a whirl or shimmer
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.InvisibleWhirl.Hint: An Invisible or Ethereal creature can't be seen, even by the GM and its owners, unless they're looking through a creature that can see it (Truesight or See Invisibility; Blindsight and Tremorsense also find Invisible creatures, and Ethereal creatures see each other). Everyone sees a whirl of air where it stands instead (a ghostly blue shimmer for an Ethereal creature), which players can target. One that is also Hiding has neither and can't be seen or targeted by players at all; the GM sees only its Hiding fog. Seen through a creature that can see it, it shows in full, with the whirl or shimmer around it unless it's Hiding. Turned off, both work like Foundry's own invisibility.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.ConditionRolls.Name: Advantage and Disadvantage from conditions
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.ConditionRolls.Hint: Apply the Advantage and Disadvantage that conditions give to attack rolls (from the attacker's conditions and the single targeted creature's, e.g. attacking a Dodging, Prone, Restrained or Invisible creature), ability checks and saving throws, on top of what dnd5e handles itself. Paralyzed, Petrified, Stunned and Unconscious creatures automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saves (the roll totals −1), and a hit on a Paralyzed or Unconscious creature from within 5 ft is a Critical Hit. A Weakened creature (Monsters of Drakkenheim, or Contamination level 4 and above) deals half damage with weapon attacks and spells. Jinxed and Valor (Monsters of Drakkenheim) take a die off or add one to attack rolls and saving throws, and bludgeoning weapon attacks against a Frozen creature are Critical Hits. Sight is judged from conditions and special senses, not walls or light. The reason is added to the roll's chat message.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.DrakkenheimAutomati: Monsters of Drakkenheim: a Bewildered creature can't cast spells other than cantrips with a casting time of an action, a Distracted one can't use anything that takes a Reaction, and a Staggered one can make only one weapon attack on its turn. A player who tries is told why; the GM is asked whether to go ahead anyway. Also, when a creature gains Drakkenheim Madness, its trait is rolled (1d10) and whispered to its owners and the GM.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.DodgeExpiry.Name: Dodging ends at the start of the creature's next turn
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.DodgeExpiry.Hint: In combat, a creature's Dodging is removed as soon as its next turn starts, as the Dodge action says. Outside combat it stays until removed.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.AutoDead.Name: Dead at 0 HP (monsters) or three failed death saves
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.AutoDead.Hint: A monster (an NPC no player owns) that drops to 0 Hit Points gets the Dead status at once, and a player character gets it when it fails its third death saving throw, so the combat tracker shows it defeated. If a monster's Hit Points go back above 0 (damage undone, healing), or a character's failures are corrected while it's still at 0 HP, that Dead status is removed again.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.StatusTooltips.Name: Status text pane
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.StatusTooltips.Hint: While the token's status palette is open, a pane beside it shows the full text of every active status effect: its name, where it comes from, how long it lasts and its description or rules. Hovering a status in the palette highlights its text. Per player.
MIGHTYGUARD.StatusPane.Title: Active statuses
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Contamination:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. Contamination is cumulative: each time you receive it you gain one or more levels. In the token's status palette, left-click the icon to add a level and right-click to remove one.

Symptoms (a creature has the symptoms of its level and every level below it):

  1. None.
  2. Halve the Hit Points you regain when you spend Hit Point Dice during a Short Rest. Applied automatically.
  3. You don't regain Hit Points when you finish a Long Rest. Applied automatically.
  4. Weakened: you deal half damage with weapon attacks and spells. Applied automatically: the Weakened status comes with this level, and your weapon and spell damage rolls are halved.
  5. Dazed: on your turn you can move or take an action, not both, and you can't take Bonus Actions. The Dazed status comes with this level, as a reminder.
  6. Monstrous Transformation: if you end your turn at 6 or more levels, you permanently become a monster controlled by the GM.

Each time you finish a Long Rest while contaminated, you roll 1d20; on a 1, you gain a level. Rolled automatically, in the chat. (These rest rules follow the GM's Contamination rest rules setting.)

Remember: each time you gain a level, roll 1d6; on a result equal to or lower than your new level, you gain a random mutation. Only Purge Contamination, Heal (all levels) and being raised from the dead (one level) remove Contamination; Lesser Restoration, Protection from Poison and Remove Curse don't.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Addled:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. You have Disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks and saving throws that use Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma.

With Advantage and Disadvantage from conditions on, this is applied to the rolls automatically.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Clumsy:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. You have Disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks and saving throws that use Dexterity.

With Advantage and Disadvantage from conditions on, this is applied to the rolls automatically.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Enfeebled:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. You have Disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks and saving throws that use Strength.

With Advantage and Disadvantage from conditions on, this is applied to the rolls automatically.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Sickened:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. You have Disadvantage on Constitution saving throws.

With Advantage and Disadvantage from conditions on, this is applied to the rolls automatically.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Defenseless:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. Attack rolls against you have Advantage.

With Advantage and Disadvantage from conditions on, this is applied to the rolls automatically.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Helpless:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. Any attack that hits you is a Critical Hit.

With Advantage and Disadvantage from conditions on, this is applied to the rolls automatically.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Weakened:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. You deal half damage with weapon attacks and spells.

With Advantage and Disadvantage from conditions on, your weapon and spell damage rolls are halved automatically (rounded down). Contamination level 4 and above gives this status.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Dazed:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. On your turn you can move or take an action, not both, and you can't take Bonus Actions.

Remember: this isn't applied automatically. Contamination level 5 and above gives this status.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Immobilized:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. Your Speed is 0 and you can't benefit from any bonus to your Speed. If you are flying, you fall.

Your Speed is set to 0 automatically.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Entangled:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. You are Immobilized and Defenseless: your Speed is 0, and attack rolls against you have Advantage.

The Immobilized and Defenseless statuses come with this one, so your Speed and the Advantage are applied automatically.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Frozen:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. You are Immobilized and Defenseless: your Speed is 0, and attack rolls against you have Advantage. Any bludgeoning weapon attack that hits you is a Critical Hit.

The Immobilized and Defenseless statuses come with this one. With Advantage and Disadvantage from conditions on, the Advantage and the Critical Hits are applied to the rolls automatically.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Shocked:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. You are Dazed and Defenseless: on your turn you can move or take an action, not both, and you can't take Bonus Actions; attack rolls against you have Advantage.

The Dazed and Defenseless statuses come with this one. The Advantage is applied automatically; Dazed is a reminder.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Jinxed:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. Jinxed (X): roll the die X and subtract it from your attack rolls and saving throws.

With Advantage and Disadvantage from conditions on, the die is taken off every attack roll and saving throw automatically, round after round. Set X in the box above (type it, or pick a die); it also shows in the effect's name, for example Jinxed (1d6). Without one it's 1d4.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Valor:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. Valor (X): roll the die X and add it to your attack rolls and saving throws.

With Advantage and Disadvantage from conditions on, the die is added to every attack roll and saving throw automatically, round after round. Set X in the box above (type it, or pick a die); it also shows in the effect's name, for example Valor (1d6). Without one it's 1d4.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Bewildered:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. You can't cast spells, except cantrips with a casting time of an action.

With Enforce Bewildered, Distracted and Staggered on, any other spell can't be cast: a player who tries is told why, and the GM is asked whether to go ahead anyway.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Distracted:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. You can't take Reactions.

With Enforce Bewildered, Distracted and Staggered on, nothing that takes a Reaction can be used (a player who tries is told why; the GM is asked whether to go ahead anyway), and Midi-QOL doesn't offer you any Reactions.

Remember: an opportunity attack is an ordinary attack taken as a Reaction, so it isn't caught: don't make one.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Staggered:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. During your turn you can make no more than one weapon attack, whatever your class features, spells or magic items would allow.

With Enforce Bewildered, Distracted and Staggered on, once you've made a weapon attack (or an unarmed strike) on your turn, another one can't be made until your next turn: a player who tries is told why, and the GM is asked whether to go ahead anyway. Attacks outside your turn aren't limited.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.DrakkenheimSlowed:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. Your Speed is halved.

Your Speed is halved automatically. (This is the Monsters of Drakkenheim condition; Slow is the spell, which does more.)
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.DrakkenheimMadness:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. You gain one of ten traits of madness, rolled with 1d10.

With Enforce Bewildered, Distracted and Staggered on, the trait is rolled when you gain this condition, written here above these rules, and whispered to you and the GM.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.ContaminationFx.Hin: Tokens with Contamination are wrapped in a slowly turning swirl of octarine light that grows brighter and reaches further in with each level. Per player.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.ExhaustionFx.Name: Bloodshot cracks on exhausted creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.ExhaustionFx.Hint: Tokens with Exhaustion get red, bloodshot cracks creeping in from their edge, reaching further in with each level. Per player.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.LevelCounters.Name: Contamination and Exhaustion counters
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.LevelCounters.Hint: Show the Contamination level in an octarine gem at the token's lower left and the Exhaustion level in a blood-red drop at its lower right, like a Hearthstone minion's Attack and Health. Per player.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.GrappleImageScale.H: The hand is fitted to the visible edge of each token's art (transparent borders around the image are ignored), so it should look the same on every token. 1 = the hand wraps the token's rim. Lower it for a smaller hand, raise it for a larger one.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.CursedFx.Name: Dark swirl on cursed creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.CursedFx.Hint: A slow swirl of dark, violet-black smoke circles just outside the token's edge, and the art dims a little.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.AddledFx.Name: A tangled thought on addled creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.AddledFx.Hint: A thought bubble floats over the creature's head with a tangled violet knot inside that keeps twisting, and question marks pop out of it.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.ClumsyFx.Name: Fumbled dagger on clumsy creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.ClumsyFx.Hint: The creature fumbles its dagger: it slips out of its hand, tumbles and clatters to the ground. Clumsy creatures roll Dexterity at Disadvantage.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.EnfeebledFx.Name: Too-heavy barbell on enfeebled creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.EnfeebledFx.Hint: The creature strains to lift a barbell, sweating and trembling, then drops it with a thud, and its art looks a little drained. Enfeebled creatures roll Strength at Disadvantage.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.SickenedFx.Name: Green fumes and flies on sickened creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.SickenedFx.Hint: Puffs of sickly green fumes rise off the creature and flies buzz around it, and the art turns a little sallow. Sickened creatures make Constitution saves at Disadvantage.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.DefenselessFx.Name: Splitting shield on defenseless creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.DefenselessFx.Hint: A shield beside the creature cracks and splits in two. Attacks against a defenseless creature have Advantage.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.HelplessFx.Name: White flag on helpless creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.HelplessFx.Hint: A white flag waves beside the creature: it can't defend itself, and any hit against it is a Critical Hit.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.ImmobilizedFx.Name: Ball and chain on immobilized creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.ImmobilizedFx.Hint: An iron cuff at the creature's feet is chained to a heavy iron ball. Every few seconds it tries to step away: the chain snaps taut and the ball scrapes along and stops it.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.EntangledFx.Name: Thorny vines on entangled creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.EntangledFx.Hint: Thorny vines burst out of a mound of torn-up earth round the creature, climb its sides and bind it across the body, squeezing now and then. They grow in when the status lands, and snap and wither away when it ends, their leaves drying up and falling.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.FrozenFx.Name: Frozen creatures turned to ice
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.FrozenFx.Hint: The creature turns to ice, pale glowing cyan, inside a thick ring of faceted ice with a strong cold glow. Splinters fly off it and frost mist rolls away. It freezes with a flash, a burst of splinters and a jolt, and cracks and shatters when the status ends.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.ShockedFx.Name: Lightning on shocked creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.ShockedFx.Hint: Bolts of lightning crackle round the creature's edge, striking a new place about three times a second, with sparks where they end, and now and then a puff of smoke rises where it's been singed.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.JinxedFx.Name: Rain cloud and unlucky die over jinxed creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.JinxedFx.Hint: A little storm cloud rains on the creature, its drops splashing on its head, and now and then drops a d20 that tumbles and lands on a 1. Jinxed creatures take a die off their attack rolls and saving throws.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.ValorFx.Name: Golden glow on creatures with Valor
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.ValorFx.Hint: A warm golden glow breathes around the creature and golden sparks rise from it.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.BewilderedFx.Name: A fizzling wand on bewildered creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.BewilderedFx.Hint: A wand at the creature's side lifts and its crystal starts to glow, but the spell sputters out in a puff of grey smoke and a few dying sparks.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.DistractedFx.Name: Wandering eye on distracted creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.DistractedFx.Hint: An eye over the creature keeps following a glint flitting about nearby: its attention is elsewhere, so it can't take Reactions.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.DazedFx.Name: Circling birds on dazed creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.DazedFx.Hint: Little birds circle over the creature's head. A dazed creature can move or take an action on its turn, not both, and no Bonus Actions. (Shocked's sparks and Stunned's stars already show it, so the birds don't.)
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.StaggeredFx.Name: Padlocked axe on staggered creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.StaggeredFx.Hint: An axe beside the creature swings once, then a padlock snaps shut on it and it can't swing again until the lock falls open. Staggered creatures can make only one weapon attack on their turn.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.WeakenedFx.Name: Wilting sword on weakened creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.WeakenedFx.Hint: A sword beside the creature goes limp and droops like a wilting flower, then perks up again. Weakened creatures deal half damage with weapon attacks and spells.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.MadnessFx.Name: Dark tendrils on creatures with Drakkenheim Madness
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.MadnessFx.Hint: Dark violet tendrils curl up from behind the creature, and now and then it twitches.
MIGHTYGUARD.Animations.Key.jinxedFx: Jinxed: rain cloud and unlucky die
MIGHTYGUARD.Animations.Key.hideAnimatedI: Hide the status icons these animations replace
MIGHTYGUARD.Animations.Name: Token animations
MIGHTYGUARD.Animations.Label: Choose Animations
MIGHTYGUARD.Animations.Hint: Turn each status animation on or off and choose whether the status icons they replace are hidden. Each player chooses for themselves. The GM also sets the Mighty Guard glow speed and the Grappled overlay here, and can give every player the same choices.
MIGHTYGUARD.Animations.Title: Token Animations
MIGHTYGUARD.Animations.Intro: These choices are yours alone: each player picks their own. Each change is saved straight away. Hover an option for details.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.SoundCues.Name: Sounds when statuses are applied
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.SoundCues.Hint: A short sound when a status lands on a creature you can see: a chime for Charmed or Hasted, a zap for Paralyzed or Stunned, a heartbeat at 0 Hit Points, a bell for Dead, and so on. Only you hear your sounds; nothing plays for creatures you can't see. Off unless you turn it on.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.SoundVolume.Name: Volume
MIGHTYGUARD.Animations.ApplyToEveryone.H: Every player's animations are set to match yours (not the animation quality, which depends on each computer). They can change their own again afterwards, and players who join later start with them.
MIGHTYGUARD.Animations.ApplyToEveryone.A: Your GM has set everyone's token animations. You can change yours in Module Settings, under Choose Animations.
MIGHTYGUARD.Animations.ApplyToEveryone.G: Every player now has your token animation choices.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.DeferToOtherModules: Leave statuses other modules animate to them

When Token Magic FX or Sequencer already animates a status on a token (for example through Convenient Effects, DAE or Automated Animations), this module adds no animation of its own for it and keeps its icon. Invisible and Ethereal creatures keep their whirl or shimmer, since that is what hides them.
MIGHTYGUARD.TokenConfig.Animations.Name: Animate this token's statuses
MIGHTYGUARD.TokenConfig.Animations.Hint: Primal Status: saved as soon as you tick or untick it, no need to press anything. Unticked, this token is shown as Foundry draws it, for everyone: its own status icons and Dead overlay, no animations, and Foundry's own invisibility. Roll rules still apply.
MIGHTYGUARD.TokenConfig.Animations.NotSa: Primal Status: couldn't save this token's animation choice. You may not have permission to change this token.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.MarkedFx.Name: Crosshairs on marked creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.MarkedFx.Hint: A red targeting reticle sits over the token: a thin ring, a crosshair with a gap at the centre and four corner brackets that close in when the mark is applied, then turn slowly while the reticle pulses gently.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.DodgingFx.Name: Afterimages on dodging creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.DodgingFx.Hint: Two blurred afterimages of the token weave from side to side and the creature itself turns slightly see-through, as if it's in several places at once.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.EtherealVision.Name: Ethereal creatures see in grey, up to 60 ft
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.EtherealVision.Hint: While a token is Ethereal, its vision turns black and white (Foundry's monochromatic vision) and reaches only 60 ft, in light or darkness, and it can't detect creatures beyond that, as on the Ethereal Plane in the 2024 rules.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.DeadSkull.Name: Big red skull on dead creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.DeadSkull.Hint: The skull Foundry shows over a Dead token is blood red and fills the whole token, instead of a smaller icon in its own colour.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.DyingFx.Name: Pulsing red skull on dying creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.DyingFx.Hint: A player character at 0 HP that isn't dead or stable shows the large red Dead skull over its token, pulsing faintly, a little stronger and quicker with each failed death save. It replaces the Unconscious Z's while the creature is dying. A monster (an NPC no player owns) at 0 HP shows the solid Dead skull straight away.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.BloodiedFx.Name: Blood splatters on bloodied creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.BloodiedFx.Hint: A few dark-red splatters and a smear appear across the token when it becomes Bloodied, each with droplets flung outward and a faint wet sheen. Each creature keeps its own pattern. Hidden while the creature is dying or dead.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.ProneFx.Name: Dust and chevrons on prone creatures
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.ProneFx.Hint: A puff of dust kicks up at the token's base when it goes Prone and settles into a low haze, while three faint downward chevrons pulse in turn over its lower half. Hidden while the creature is dying or dead.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.AnimationQuality.Hi: Full: every animation moves smoothly. Reduced: about 30 updates a second with lighter blurs, easier on slower computers. Still: each animation is shown settled and doesn't move, redrawn only when something changes. Automatic uses Still if your system asks for reduced motion, otherwise Full.
MIGHTYGUARD.Migrate.Done: Primal Status: carried over {settings} settings, {images} status images and {macros} macros from the module's earlier ID (Enhanced Status Effects or Mighty Guard).

MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.ContaminationRest.H: Monsters of Drakkenheim. After a long rest, each contaminated creature rolls 1d20 in the chat and gains a level on a 1. From level 2, Hit Point Dice heal half as much; from level 3, a long rest restores no Hit Points.
MIGHTYGUARD.ContaminationRest.Gained: {name} rolled a 1 after the long rest and is now at level {level}.
MIGHTYGUARD.ContaminationRest.Safe: {name} finished a long rest without gaining a level.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Burning:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. Burning (X): you're on fire, or covered in acid. At the end of each of your turns you take X damage, fire or acid. Without an X it's 1d4 fire.

It ends when you, or a creature within 5 feet of you, takes an action to put out the flames or scrape off the acid, or when something else douses the flames (being submerged in water, for example).

Pick Fire or Acid above, and set X in the box (type it, or pick one); both show in the effect's name, for example Burning (2d4 Acid). A creature burning with acid gets a green, dripping aura instead of flames. With Burning and Bleeding at the end of each turn on, the damage is rolled in the chat at the end of each of your turns in combat, and taken off your Hit Points (counting your resistances and immunities) if the GM chose that.

Remember: putting it out isn't automatic: remove the condition when it's done.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desc.Bleeding:
Monsters of Drakkenheim. Bleeding (X): you're losing blood from an open wound. At the end of each of your turns you lose X Hit Points. Without an X it's 1d4.

It ends when you regain any Hit Points, or when you, or a creature within 5 feet of you, takes an action to use a healer's kit on you (no check needed).

Set X in the box above (type it, or pick a die); it also shows in the effect's name, for example Bleeding (2d4). With Burning and Bleeding at the end of each turn on, X is rolled in the chat at the end of each of your turns in combat and taken off your Hit Points if the GM chose that (lost, so resistances don't count), and the condition ends by itself when you regain Hit Points.

Remember: the healer's kit isn't automatic: remove the condition when it's used.

MIGHTYGUARD.Madness.Trait1: Is sure the organs inside them are useless, and wishes they were gone.
MIGHTYGUARD.Madness.Trait2: Sees the contamination as a gift that will change them into something wondrous.
MIGHTYGUARD.Madness.Trait3: Believes the monsters are peaceful townsfolk who need protecting.
MIGHTYGUARD.Madness.Trait4: Wants to wear the skins of slain enemies to take their strength.
MIGHTYGUARD.Madness.Trait5: Believes their companions died in the ruins and are only ghosts, and won't let them talk to anyone else.
MIGHTYGUARD.Madness.Trait6: Eats everything they can find, sure that each meal is their last.
MIGHTYGUARD.Madness.Trait7: Is enchanted by Drakkenheim by moonlight and wants to roam its streets every night.
MIGHTYGUARD.Madness.Trait8: Insists that anyone who dies in Drakkenheim dies in real life, too.
MIGHTYGUARD.Madness.Trait9: Is sure a secret cabal of disembodied hands is plotting against them.
MIGHTYGUARD.Madness.Trait10: Feels driven to go into the ruins and kill, again and again, until it's done.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.SaveEndsCombatEnd.N: Short save-ends effects end with the combat
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.SaveEndsCombatEnd.H: When a combat ends, every effect on its creatures that lasts 1 minute or less and ends on a successful saving throw is removed (for example Hold Person's Paralyzed). An effect counts as ending on a save when it has a Midi-QOL OverTime save, a DAE save special duration, or its text or its item's description says so ("…repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success").
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.BurningDamage.Name: Burning and Bleeding at the end of each turn
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.BurningDamage.Hint: In combat, at the end of each of a creature's turns, a Burning creature's damage (its X: fire, or the type its X names, such as 2d4 Acid) and a Bleeding creature's lost Hit Points (its X) are rolled in the chat. "Roll and apply" also takes them off its Hit Points (Burning counts resistances and immunities; Bleeding's Hit Points are simply lost). Unless this is Off, a Bleeding creature stops bleeding when it regains Hit Points.
When a player's character is at 10% of its Hit Points or less, the first attack roll it makes each turn in combat has a chance (Desperation attack chance, below) of becoming a Desperation Attack: it hits automatically (never as a critical hit) and deals 1.5 times its maximum damage. The chat card only calls it a Desperation Attack, coloured to stand out, and doesn't explain it; players don't see the dice or formula on it. Players never see this setting.
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.DesperationChance.N: Desperation attack chance, in % (hidden from players)
MIGHTYGUARD.Settings.DesperationChance.H: How likely that first attack roll is to become a Desperation Attack: 0 never, 100 every time, 50 by default. Only used while Desperation attacks is on. Players never see this setting.
MIGHTYGUARD.Desperation.Name: Desperation Attack
